title: Eviction: resource pressure and what the cluster drops first

videos.script: A pod is evicted when the cluster decides it should not run where it is. That happens for three reasons, and they look different from the outside. {{three}} A node can run short of memory or disk, and the kubelet removes pods to save the node. {{pressure}} A person can take a node out for maintenance, and the cluster has to move its pods without breaking the application. {{drain}} And a node can simply disappear, and the rest of the cluster has to notice and start the copies elsewhere. {{lost}} You will see all three: a pod that fills its disk, a drain held back by a budget, and a node switched off without warning. {{plan}}
